title: A Systematic Review of Demand Forecasting Models for Retail E-Commerce Enhancing Accuracy in Inventory and Delivery Planning
authors: Chowdhury, A. R.; Paul, R.; Rozony, F. Z.
venue: International Journal of Scientific Interdisciplinary Research
tldr: A systematic review of 72 studies evaluates traditional statistical, machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid demand forecasting models for retail e-commerce, finding that ML and deep learning models significantly outperform classical methods in volatile environments.
problem_and_motivation: Retail e-commerce demand forecasting faces unique challenges including volatile consumer behavior, high product turnover, and omnichannel complexity that traditional models cannot adequately address. There is a lack of comprehensive synthesis comparing the effectiveness and contextual suitability of diverse forecasting methodologies. Organizations need a consolidated knowledge base to select appropriate models aligned with their technological infrastructure.
approach: Conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of 72 peer-reviewed articles published between 2010 and 2024 from databases including Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect.
Categorized forecasting models into four categories: traditional statistical, machine learning, hybrid, and deep learning architectures.
Extracted key data using a structured coding framework covering forecasting techniques, dataset characteristics, accuracy metrics, and external variables.
Synthesized findings thematically to compare model performance across different demand patterns and forecasting horizons.
Assessed models based on MAE, RMSE, MAPE, and practical implementation criteria including computational cost and interpretability.
findings: Traditional statistical models (ARIMA, SARIMA, Holt-Winters) were used in 21 of 72 studies with over 2,300 cumulative citations, maintaining relevance for stable demand patterns.
Machine learning models appeared in 31 studies with over 4,800 citations, improving accuracy metrics by up to 20% over statistical methods in short to medium-term forecasting.
Deep learning models (LSTM, GRU, CNN, Transformers) were used in 22 studies with over 3,900 citations, excelling at capturing long-term dependencies and nonlinear patterns.
Hybrid models combining statistical and AI methods were evaluated in 18 studies with approximately 2,500 citations, offering balanced interpretability and predictive accuracy.
External data integration (weather, sentiment, economic indicators) appeared in 27 studies with over 5,000 citations, significantly enhancing forecast accuracy in volatile categories.
num: A 10% improvement in forecast accuracy could reduce inventory costs by up to 25%.
num: Deep learning models reduced overstock rates in high-SKU environments by up to 15%.
Ensemble models combining multiple forecasting approaches consistently outperformed individual learners across diverse demand patterns.

key_equations.explanation: Mean Absolute Error measures average magnitude of forecast errors without considering direction.
Root Mean Squared Error penalizes larger forecast errors more heavily than MAE.
Mean Absolute Percentage Error provides scale-independent accuracy comparison across products.

definitions.definition: AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average, a classical time series model incorporating autoregression, differencing, and moving averages for non-stationary data.
Seasonal ARIMA, an extension of ARIMA that accounts for seasonal patterns in time series data.
Long Short-Term Memory, a recurrent neural network architecture designed to capture long-range temporal dependencies.
Gated Recurrent Unit, a simplified RNN variant with gating mechanisms for efficient sequence learning.
Convolutional Neural Network, adapted for time series to capture local patterns through convolutional operations.
Support Vector Regression, an extension of SVM for regression tasks using hyperplane construction in high-dimensional space.
Mean Absolute Percentage Error, a scale-independent metric for evaluating forecast accuracy across products of varying demand levels.
Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses, a guideline framework for conducting transparent systematic reviews.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This systematic review provides a comprehensive taxonomy of demand forecasting methodologies spanning traditional statistical models through advanced deep learning architectures. It establishes empirical benchmarks across 72 studies, demonstrating that machine learning and hybrid models significantly outperform classical approaches in volatile environments. The review identifies external data integration as a critical differentiator in forecast accuracy. It offers a methodological foundation for selecting and combining forecasting approaches based on data characteristics and operational requirements.
directly_justifies: LSTM and GRU models capture long-range temporal dependencies superior to traditional time series methods.
Hybrid ARIMA-ML models consistently outperform standalone approaches in volatile demand scenarios.
External data integration from weather, sentiment, and economic indicators significantly enhances forecast accuracy.
A 10% improvement in forecast accuracy reduces inventory costs by up to 25%.
Deep learning models reduced overstock rates in high-SKU environments by up to 15%.
limits: Review limited to English-language peer-reviewed publications, potentially excluding relevant non-English studies.
Most studies reviewed used proprietary e-commerce datasets, limiting reproducibility.
Computational cost comparisons across models were inconsistent across reviewed studies.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domains 6.A and 6.B were flagged as high relevance due to the paper's core focus on predictive modeling and sequential data forecasting algorithms. Domain 8.A received medium relevance as the paper discusses demand spike detection relevant to anomaly identification. Domains 12.A and 12.B received medium relevance for their evaluation framework contributions. Domain 13.A received low relevance due to the parallel between inventory optimization and savings management. Domain 13.B was contextual only, as forecasting methodologies could theoretically inform debt scheduling. Domains 1.A through 5.C were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, financial behavior, or expense categorization. Domains 7.A through 7.E were rejected as budgeting strategies are not discussed. Domains 9.A through 11.B were rejected as the paper does not cover mobile design, privacy, or engagement. Domain 14.A was rejected as synthetic data generation is not addressed. The paper's overall topical coverage centers on predictive modeling and forecasting algorithm evaluation.

limitations: Review limited to English-language publications, potentially excluding relevant international studies in other languages.
Most reviewed studies used proprietary e-commerce datasets, limiting reproducibility and generalizability.
Computational cost and latency comparisons were inconsistently reported across studies.
The paper does not address implementation challenges for small and medium enterprises with limited infrastructure.
remember_this: Machine learning models improve forecast accuracy by up to 20% over traditional statistical methods.
Hybrid ARIMA-ML models offer the best balance of interpretability and predictive accuracy.
External data integration including sentiment and weather significantly enhances forecast performance.
Deep learning models excel at capturing nonlinear demand patterns but require substantial computational resources.
A 10% forecast accuracy improvement can reduce inventory costs by up to 25%.
